data.one_liner: Spring animations and physics simulations simplified for Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Provides builders, draggable widgets, and simulation controllers for 1D and 2D spring-based animations and physics in Flutter. Offers preset spring configurations like bouncy, snappy, and interactive.
use_when: You want spring-based animations with natural physics and customizable bounce or duration.
You need widgets that can be dragged and return to their origin with a spring animation.
You need low-level spring simulation controllers similar to AnimationController.
avoid_when: You want the next-generation package Motor, which supersedes Springster with a unified motion API.
You require complex multi-dimensional animations with independent physics per dimension (use Motor instead).
strengths: Simple declarative widgets like SpringBuilder and SpringBuilder2D.
Includes 2D spring animations and SpringDraggable out of the box.
Multiple predefined spring configurations (bouncy, snappy, instant, etc.).
weaknesses: Deprecated in favor of the newer Motor package.
Limited to spring physics and basic simulation controllers.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need complex vector animations exported from After Effects.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a comprehensive chained animation extension syntax over physics-based springs.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you require interactive state-machine driven vector graphics.
